newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans seen 3-5 cents lower on USDA data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans seen 3-5 cents lower on USDA data.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures were expected to open three to five cents per bushel lower Thursday in response to supply and demand data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, traders said.
In its latest report, USDA raised the old-crop soybean end stocks by five million bushels to 130 million, and left Brazilian soybean production unchanged at 26.50 million tonnes.
Some in the trade expected USDA to lower the Brazil crop estimate because of a late-season drought.
Total net soybean export sales were judged mediocre by traders and were seen having little influence on prices.
USDA put old crop sales at a small 41,400 tonnes, and new crop sales were 572,400 tonnes. Traders were expecting old crop sales of 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes.
